newsitem.title: UK: SOCCER-ADAMS REPORTED TO HAVE CONFESSED TO ALCOHOLISM.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-ADAMS REPORTED TO HAVE CONFESSED TO ALCOHOLISM.

text.p: Former England soccer captain Tony Adams has reportedly confessed to his Arsenal team mates that he is an alcoholic.
Adams, 30 next month, was said to have told of his drink problem at a meeting with fellow players on Friday.
The news is the latest major blow for Arsenal, beleaguered by the recent loss of not only their manager Bruce Rioch but their stand-in coach Stewart Houston.
Adams is said to have told players he hoped for the same support that Arsenal striker Paul Merson received when he admitted he was addicted to drink, drugs and gambling.
Merson was said to have been the first team mate to offer his help, telling Adams he would support him in his bid to cure the drink problem.
On Saturday, a close friend of both players, said: "The biggest hurdle is admitting the problem and Tony realises there is a very big battle ahead.
"But he is a man who has led his country so there is no doubt about his strength and commitment to face up to reality."
Adams has not played this season because of a knee injury.
His wife Jane has been in rehabilitation for a drugs problem and it has been reported recently that he is seeking a divorce. The couple have three children.

Adams, who has won 45 England caps, was reported in British newspapers on Saturday to have made his confession at a meeting of the players called by Arsenal's new caretaker manager Pat Rice, who was appointed on Friday.
His team mates were well aware of his problems with drink. In December 1990 he was jailed for four months for drink-driving following a crash.

In 1993 he needed stitches to a head wound after falling down stairs at a nightclub. Later that year he was involved with a team mate in an incident at a pizza restaurant when customers were sprayed with a fire extinguisher.
This year -- on Cup Final day -- he was reported to have gone on a 16-hour pub crawl, ending up on stage with a stripper.
But his record on the pitch has been impressive, leading Arsenal to two league championships, two league cup victories, an F.A. Cup final triumph and success in the European Cup Winners' Cup.
He also skippered England throughout this summers Euro 96 campaign which saw them lose on penalties to Germany in the semifinal.
